source_review.notes: Checked current ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-1:2022 definitions and oracle scope through the official ISO record/preview, IEEE Computer Society SWEBOK v4.0a testing material, and the primary Barr et al. oracle-problem survey. Foundational testing texts support durable exact, model, relational, differential, and human-oracle claims.

evidence: Reviewed conditional expectation, accepted-set, observation projection, four-verdict oracle, tolerance, soundness/completeness, and predicate-conjunction notation.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Symbols are defined before use and scoped to a versioned basis, item, case, environment, and observation boundary.

evidence: Executed transfer-oracle-verdicts and independently verified 100 minus 30 equals 70, audit counts, and summary counts PASS=1, FAIL=1, INCONCLUSIVE=1.
Rechecked the absolute-plus-relative tolerance expression across near-zero and large-magnitude cases conceptually.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The transfer arithmetic is a teaching predicate only; no real financial/accounting adequacy is inferred.

evidence: Re-derived accepted observations from versioned predicates and the four-case oracle mapping.
Checked observation projection and required/forbidden/permitted/unspecified distinctions.
Re-derived conjunction behavior with unknown evidence propagation.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The formalism models verdict semantics and never claims that the basis, observation, or oracle is universally sound or complete.

evidence: Reviewed missing observation, ambiguous/conflicting basis, oracle execution error, forbidden side effects, unspecified ordering, duplicate/missing events, retry, nondeterministic histories, time windows, near-zero/large floating values, NaN/infinity, reference correlation, stale snapshots, and high-stakes transfer cases.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Unknown evidence never becomes pass; boundary cases distinguish product failure from oracle/test failure.

evidence: Traced claim-to-oracle linkage, explicit observation boundary, source provenance, no unknown-to-pass coercion, common-mode analysis, non-compensable conjunction, and authority proportional to consequence through examples and answers.
invariant_checking.notes: Every oracle type is labeled partial or assumption-bound; passing encoded expectations remains distinct from fitness validation.

evidence: Reviewed the membership-based verdict cases and transfer-oracle decision branches line by line.
Checked sound-for-rejection and complete-for-rejection definitions relative to a stated model.
proof_review.notes: No universal product-correctness proof is claimed; definitions are conditional on a valid model, basis, observation, and oracle execution.

evidence: Audited uses of proves, correct, sound, complete, exact, permitted, expected, pass, valid, and truth.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No proof sketch is presented; exact and model-derived results retain source and assumption limits.

evidence: Reviewed executable-output scope, current-standard claims, differential/metamorphic evidence, stochastic statements, human-oracle limits, and clinical/railway disclaimers.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The snippet validates deterministic verdict propagation only. No empirical effectiveness, certification, safety, or external-review claim is made.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed test basis, expectations, accepted sets, observation, oracle taxonomy, partiality, verdict logic, independence, approximate/time/stochastic behavior, human authority, and oracle testing for conceptual coherence.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed snapshot/refactoring workflow, side-effect observations, model/reference independence, retry/idempotency, error and inconclusive routing, negative controls, provenance, and high-consequence escalation. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from basis and accepted sets through oracle families and four-valued logic to portfolio assurance; ten examples and five complete answers provide distinct retrieval, diagnosis, comparison, and safety-transfer practice.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
